question: The fraud-reporting template our Toronto office received from a U.S. branch points to a U.S. reporting page. Where should the Canadian version direct readers for reporting a suspected scam in Canada?
generated_answer:
The original template directs users to a U.S. reporting page. However, it is important to direct Canadians to the appropriate Canadian reporting agency for reporting a suspected scam. The original text should be edited to include a link to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (CAFC) or another relevant Canadian reporting agency. For example:

"Please report any suspected scam to the appropriate authorities. In Canada, you can report to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (CAFC) at [CAFC website or phone number]. If you are in the U.S., please report to [U.S. reporting agency] at [U.S. reporting page]."

This ensures that Canadians are directed to the correct reporting agency in their country. 

The CAFC website is: [https://www.antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/index-eng.htm](https://www.antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/index-eng.htm)

Their phone number is: 1-888-495-8501 (toll-free)

Please note that the website or phone number may have changed since the last update, so it's best to verify the current information from the CAFC website or directly from the CAFC.

---

**Revised template for Canadian offices:**

Please report any suspected scam to the appropriate authorities. In Canada, you can report to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre (CAFC) at [https://www.antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/index-eng.htm](https://www.antifraudcentre-centreantifraude.ca/index-eng.htm) or call 1-888-495-8501 (toll-free). If you are in the U.S., please report to [U.S. reporting agency] at [U.S. reporting page]. 

--- 

**Note for future reference:** Always verify the current reporting information from official sources to ensure accuracy. In this case, you should check the CAFC website for the most up-to-date reporting instructions and contact information. 

---

If the template is being shared across offices in multiple countries, it's best to have separate versions for each country, each directing users to the relevant national reporting agency. This ensures that all users receive accurate and relevant information for reporting scams in their respective countries. 

If you need further assistance or have more specific questions about the template or reporting process, please let me know!
